promptLatex: Let $D_n$ be the number of derangements of $n$ objects, that is, permutations in which no object stays in its original position. What are the last three digits of $D_{12}$?
hintLatex: Everything can be done modulo $1000$, which keeps the arithmetic small.
Either iterate the two-term recurrence or use the one-step form $D_n = n D_{n-1} + (-1)^n$.
Reduce at every step; the last three digits of a sum depend only on the last three digits of the summands.
solutionLatex:
Since the recurrence uses only addition and multiplication, reducing modulo $1000$ at every step gives the last three digits exactly. Using $D_n = n D_{n-1} + (-1)^n$ from $D_1 = 0$:

$D_2 \equiv 1$, $D_3 \equiv 3 \cdot 1 - 1 = 2$, $D_4 \equiv 4 \cdot 2 + 1 = 9$, $D_5 \equiv 5 \cdot 9 - 1 = 44$, $D_6 \equiv 6 \cdot 44 + 1 = 265$, $D_7 \equiv 7 \cdot 265 - 1 = 1854 \equiv 854$, $D_8 \equiv 8 \cdot 854 + 1 = 6833 \equiv 833$, $D_9 \equiv 9 \cdot 833 - 1 = 7496 \equiv 496$, $D_{10} \equiv 10 \cdot 496 + 1 = 4961 \equiv 961$, $D_{11} \equiv 11 \cdot 961 - 1 = 10570 \equiv 570$, $D_{12} \equiv 12 \cdot 570 + 1 = 6841 \equiv 841$.

So the last three digits of $D_{12}$ are $841$. As a check, the exact values are $D_{10} = 1334961$, $D_{11} = 14684570$, and $D_{12} = 176214841$.
